A_USS.name: USS - User Satisfaction Simulation (Sun et al., SIGIR 2021, arXiv 2105.03748)
A_USS.licence: GitHub repo: NO LICENSE file found (raw LICENSE -> 404). HF mirror card declares MIT (stated by the mirror uploader, not by the authors). Underlying corpora have their own terms (SGD CC-BY-SA-4.0, MultiWOZ MIT, ReDial CC-BY-4.0, CCPE CC-BY-SA-4.0, JDDC research-only per JD.com). Verdict: academic research use with citation; do not redistribute raw text.
A_USS.why_original_not_mirror: the HF mirror is parquet (no parquet reader in the venv) and has only 4 EN sub-datasets; the original TXT has per-annotator ratings for all 5 sub-datasets incl. JDDC. The mirror parquet was downloaded (sha256 b1337c9c00617e7df4f72cad1f3e99573badf5bea30e18a560fdfbe6b58c2b00, 2.3 MB) but its rows were NOT VERIFIED (not parsed); its card reports 3,500 dialogs / 34,358 turns.
A_USS.schema: TXT, one utterance per line: ROLE \t text \t action \t ratings 'a,b,c' (USER lines) [\t explanation]; dialogues separated by blank lines; last line 'USER \t OVERALL \t \t r1,r2,..' = dialogue-level rating.
A_USS.label_semantics: 1-5 user satisfaction judged by crowd/expert annotators reading the dialogue (third-party judgement, NOT self-reported by the real user). Turn level: satisfaction at each user turn (with the preceding system response). Dialogue level (OVERALL): satisfaction with the whole dialogue.
A_USS.agent_f_target: mean of the annotators' OVERALL ratings; predicted after the dialogue ends from the full dialogue text
A_USS.domain: SGD/MWOZ: task-oriented assistants (booking, travel, weather...); ReDial: movie recommendation; CCPE: preference elicitation (movies); JDDC: REAL e-commerce customer service chats (JD.com) - closest to ShopNova.
A_USS.grouping_key: (sub-dataset, dialogue index in file); one example = one dialogue, so turns never cross splits

split.rule: 70/15/15 by dialogue, stratified per sub-dataset, seed 13

A_USS.duplicates: exact duplicate dialogue texts: JDDC 28 (dropped, first kept), others 0
A_USS.inter_annotator: 3-7 annotators per dialogue (EN), exactly 3 (JDDC). Krippendorff alpha (interval) on OVERALL: SGD 0.225, MWOZ 0.199, ReDial 0.28, CCPE 0.202, JDDC 0.524 (see per_subdataset). EN labels are concentrated on 3 (std of the mean rating 0.35-0.45) and noisy.
A_USS.verdict: USABLE as the PRIMARY public benchmark for dialogue-level satisfaction (EN and ZH reported separately). Caveats: annotator (not customer) judgements; EN sub-datasets are not customer support; low EN agreement limits achievable accuracy; JDDC is genuine e-commerce support but Chinese (no FR).

D_Saif7800_customer_qa.name: Saif7800/customer_qa_dataset
D_Saif7800_customer_qa.size: train 1,365,546,421 B (450,724 rows), validation 79,667,470 B (24,988), test 79,653,461 B (24,988) - too big; only the first 3,000,000 bytes of validation_complete.jsonl were fetched (939 rows parsed)
D_Saif7800_customer_qa.schema: 29 columns incl. conversation[{role,text}], language, domain, sentiment, resolution, csat (1-5), quality_score

observations_on_939_rows.csat_vs_sentiment: urgent->3 (208/208), confused->3 (208/208), frustrated->2 (109) or 3 (58), neutral->4 (193) or 3 (13), positive->4 (80) or 5 (70): csat is (almost) a deterministic function of the sentiment tag

D_Saif7800_customer_qa.verdict: SYNTHETIC (LLM-generated), labels rule-derived from a sentiment tag; 'unresolved' conversations get csat 4-5 often. NOT USED for training or evaluation. At most a clearly-labelled synthetic smoke test (format checks).
